name: Gravity I2C ozone sensor (DFRobot SEN0321)
description: Electrochemical ozone (O3) sensor module, 0-10 ppm with 10 ppb resolution: a Winsen ZE27-O3 cell module read by an onboard STM8 that presents the concentration over I2C as a 16-bit ppb value. Supply 3.3-5.5 V (onboard boost and 3 V regulator), 3 min warm-up, response time <= 90 s. I2C address 0x70-0x73 set by the A0/A1 DIP switch. Sold as: DFRobot Gravity: I2C Ozone Sensor (0-10ppm), SKU SEN0321, 4-pin Gravity I2C connector SDA, SCL, GND, VCC.
eli5: Smells the air for ozone, the sharp-smelling gas made by ozone generators, UV lamps and smog, and tells your board how much is there in parts per billion.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pin 1). MOSFET level shifter with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board, so the bus idles at VCC.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pin 2). MOSFET level shifter with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3.3-5.5 V (pin 4, red wire). Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico: the I2C pull-ups go to VCC.

supplierQuery: DFRobot SEN0321 Gravity I2C ozone sensor 0-10ppm
buildNotes: Connector order (DFRobot pinout table and schematic P1): 1 SDA, 2 SCL, 3 GND, 4 VCC. The real board has a 4-pin PH2.0 Gravity socket; use the supplied cable or Dupont adapters.
Power VCC from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico: SDA and SCL have 10 kOhm pull-ups to VCC behind the MOSFET level shifters, so a 5 V supply would put 5 V on the bus.
I2C address from the A0/A1 DIP switch: 0x70 [0 0], 0x71 [1 0], 0x72 [0 1], 0x73 [1 1]. DFRobot's example uses 0x73; run i2c.scan() if unsure.

Read sequence (DFRobot library): write 0x03 = 0x01 for passive mode once; then per reading write 0x04 = 0x01, wait 100 ms, write the pointer 0x07, wait 100 ms, read 2 bytes. ppb = high * 256 + low. In active mode (0x03 = 0x00) request with 0x04 = 0x00 and read from 0x09.
Let the electrochemical cell warm up at least 3 minutes after power-on before trusting readings; response and recovery take up to 90 s.
Ozone is toxic: the 8-hour workplace limit is around 0.1 ppm (100 ppb). Test with good ventilation and do not run ozone generators near people.
Do not expose the cell to high concentrations of alcohol or other interfering gases; keep it in 15-90 %RH, -20 to 50 C, no condensation.

driver.code:
# DFRobot Gravity I2C ozone sensor (SEN0321, Winsen ZE27-O3 behind an STM8 I2C bridge), MicroPython driver.
# Register map and sequences from DFRobot's DFRobot_OzoneSensor library:
#   0x03 MODE      0x00 = active (sensor uploads every second), 0x01 = passive (read on request)
#   0x04 REQUEST   write 0x00 in active mode, 0x01 in passive mode to fetch a new value
#   0x07/0x08      passive-mode concentration, high byte first, ppb
#   0x09/0x0A      active-mode concentration, high byte first, ppb
# Ozone (ppb) = high * 256 + low; ppm = ppb / 1000. Range 0-10 ppm, resolution 10 ppb.
import time

MODE_ACTIVE = 0x00
MODE_PASSIVE = 0x01

_REG_MODE = 0x03
_REG_REQUEST = 0x04
_REG_PASSIVE_DATA = 0x07
_REG_ACTIVE_DATA = 0x09


class GravityOzone:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x73, mode=MODE_PASSIVE):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.set_mode(mode)

    def set_mode(self, mode):
        if mode not in (MODE_ACTIVE, MODE_PASSIVE):
            raise ValueError('mode must be MODE_ACTIVE or MODE_PASSIVE')
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([_REG_MODE, mode]))
        time.sleep_ms(100)  # the bridge MCU forwards the mode command to the ZE27-O3 over UART
        self.mode = mode

    def _read_word(self, reg):
        # Same sequence as DFRobot's library: set the register pointer (with STOP), wait, then read 2 bytes.
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([reg]))
        time.sleep_ms(100)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def read_ppb(self):
        """Ozone concentration in ppb (parts per billion)."""
        if self.mode == MODE_PASSIVE:
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([_REG_REQUEST, 0x01]))  # request one reading
            time.sleep_ms(100)
            return self._read_word(_REG_PASSIVE_DATA)
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([_REG_REQUEST, 0x00]))
        time.sleep_ms(100)
        return self._read_word(_REG_ACTIVE_DATA)

    def read_ppm(self):
        return self.read_ppb() / 1000

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from gravity_ozone import GravityOzone

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = GravityOzone(i2c, addr=0x73)
while True:
    ppb = sensor.read_ppb()
    print('O3=%dppb %.2fppm' % (ppb, ppb / 1000))
    time.sleep(1)
